N-2.1-A.skill: classify the bonding in a solid from a set of property data, resisting a single misleading cue (low melting temperature)

N-2.1-B.skill: use electronegativity values to determine the direction of bond polarity, including cases where hydrogen is the more electronegative atom

N-2.2-A.skill: read bond length (position of the minimum) and bond energy (depth of the minimum) from potential-energy data, without assuming that the shorter bond is the stronger one

N-2.2-B.skill: use a potential-energy curve to predict the direction of the net force and the motion of two atoms released from rest at a given distance

N-2.3-A.skill: apply Coulomb's law quantitatively, using ion charges and the sum of ionic radii, to compare the strength of ionic attractions in two crystals

N-2.3-B.skill: explain electrical conductivity data for an ionic compound in terms of mobile charged particles in the lattice, liquid and solution

N-2.4-A.skill: use atomic radii to identify the type of alloy and explain the change in hardness at the particle level

N-2.4-B.skill: explain trends in metallic melting temperature using the number of delocalized electrons per atom and the size of the metal cores

N-2.5-A.skill: build a Lewis diagram from the valence electron count and count all nonbonding pairs, including the extra pairs on an expanded-octet central atom

N-2.5-B.skill: deduce the number of shared electron pairs between two atoms from the formula by combining the valence electron count and the octet rule

N-2.6-A.skill: use all resonance contributors to predict the average bond order and the average formal charge on equivalent atoms

N-2.6-B.skill: distinguish formal charge from oxidation number for the same atom in the same species

N-2.7-A.skill: count sigma and pi bonds and assign hybridization for several atoms in a molecule from its bonding pattern

N-2.7-B.skill: use electron-domain repulsion, including the greater repulsion of lone pairs, to explain observed deviations in bond angle
